content.value_statement: Teams need consistent handoffs between development, testing, review, and merge phases. This skill validates allowed transitions, delegates thread changes, and updates workflow memory.
actual_capabilities: Defines valid DEV, TEST, REVIEW, and merge transitions.
Blocks DEV to REVIEW and REVIEW to TEST transitions.
Runs a phase-gate check before transition execution.
Delegates current thread closing to the matching thread manager.
Requests memory synchronization after a transition.
Reports transition results with thread, link, and memory status.
limitations: It does not save progress without changing phases.
It depends on phase-gate and thread-manager agents being available.
It does not define GitHub API credentials or authentication setup.
It may write to configured workflow files and settings.

use_cases.title: Promote completed development work
use_cases.description: Move a finished DEV thread into TEST after implementation and test preparation are complete.

use_cases.title: Send tested work to review
use_cases.description: Move a TEST thread into REVIEW only after the phase gate confirms passing tests.

use_cases.title: Demote failed review work
use_cases.description: Return REVIEW work to DEV when a fail verdict requires structural changes.

prompt_templates.title: Move DEV to TEST
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard promotion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Move this GitHub Elements item from DEV to TEST. Validate the phase gate first and report any blocker.

prompt_templates.title: Move TEST to REVIEW
prompt_templates.prompt: Transition the current TEST thread to REVIEW after confirming all tests pass and completion comments exist.

prompt_templates.title: Demote failed REVIEW
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a review failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Demote this REVIEW thread to DEV because the review verdict failed. Close the current thread and link the next one.

prompt_templates.title: Complete REVIEW pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced merge transition with full reporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transition this REVIEW thread to merge after a PASS verdict. Include phase-gate results, thread changes, links, and memory-sync status.

output_examples.input: Move a completed DEV item to TEST.
output_examples.output: Phase gate passed. The DEV thread was closed, the TEST thread was opened, links were established, and memory was updated.

output_examples.input: Move TEST work to REVIEW before tests pass.
output_examples.output: Transition blocked. The phase gate found missing test completion evidence, so no thread changes were made.

output_examples.input: Demote a failed REVIEW item to DEV.
output_examples.output: Review demotion completed. The REVIEW thread was closed, a DEV thread was opened, links were recorded, and memory was synced.

best_practices: Run it only when the current phase is complete.
Confirm tests or review verdicts before requesting a transition.
Review phase-gate blockers before retrying a transition.
anti_patterns: Using it as a progress checkpoint.
Skipping failed validation to force a handoff.
Requesting a direct DEV to REVIEW transition.

faq.question: Can this skill save progress without changing phases?
faq.answer: No. It is for phase transitions. Use the checkpoint workflow for progress updates.

faq.question: Which transitions are valid?
faq.answer: It supports DEV to TEST, TEST to REVIEW, TEST to DEV, REVIEW to DEV, and REVIEW to merge.

faq.question: Does it validate transitions before making changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs a phase-gate check before closing or opening workflow threads.

faq.question: What happens when validation fails?
faq.answer: The transition is blocked, the reason is reported, and no thread change should proceed.

faq.question: Does it create or close GitHub issue threads directly?
faq.answer: It delegates thread work to the matching DEV, TEST, or REVIEW thread manager.

faq.question: Does it use local settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It references .claude/ghe.local.md for enablement, enforcement level, and memory-sync behavior.
